name: Solid-State Chemistry and Materials Design
description:
Crystalline Solids: Structure and Description
Concept of the crystal as a convolution of lattice and motif; crystal systems and Bravais lattices; lattice planes and Miller indices. Representation of crystal structures using fractional atomic coordinates. Construction and interpretation of Crystallographic Information Files (CIFs) for visualization and analysis.
Symmetry in the Solid State
Symmetry elements and operations; point groups and space groups; their significance in crystal classification and property determination.
Representative Crystal Structures
Detailed study of important structure types including perovskites, hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites, spinels, rutile, and CdCl₂-type structures. Correlation between atomic arrangement, bonding, and physical properties.
Thermodynamics and Energetics of Solids
Thermodynamics of crystal formation; lattice energy estimation; ionic radii and radius ratio rules; stability of ionic and molecular solids.
Polymorphism and Computational Approaches
Structural diversity in molecular solids; principles of polymorphism and phase transformations. Computational methods for predicting solid-state properties, lattice stability, intermolecular interactions, and analysis of voids and channels.
Defects and Disorder in Crystals
Classification and types of defects—point, line, and planar; static and dynamic disorder. Defect chemistry in ionic, covalent, and metallic solids and their influence on materials properties.
Synthesis of Functional Solids and Nanomaterials
Solid-state reactions; Chimie Douce methods; sol–gel synthesis; synthesis of nanoparticles and quantum dots. Design and synthesis of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and porous materials.
Characterization Techniques
Structural characterization by X-ray diffraction (XRD): powder diffraction for phase identification and crystallite size determination; structure solution using single-crystal XRD.
Electronic Structure and Band Theory
Energy bands in solids—valence and conduction bands, Fermi level, Bloch’s theorem, and E–k diagrams. Direct and indirect band gap materials; classification as insulators, semiconductors, conductors, and superconductors. Effect of doping on band structure; experimental methods for band gap estimation.
Optical and Electronic Properties of Nanostructured Materials
Origin of optical and electronic properties in nanoparticles and quantum dots; surface plasmon resonance and its applications in sensing and catalysis.
Electrical and Functional Properties of Solids
Electrical conductivity in metals, semiconductors, and insulators. Structure–symmetry–property relationships in ferroelectric, dielectric, thermoelectric, and piezoelectric materials.
Magnetic Properties of Materials
Origin of magnetism in solids; types of magnetic behavior—paramagnetism, diamagnetism, ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, and ferrimagnetism; structure–property correlations.
Structure–Function Relationships and Applications
Design principles of materials for applications in batteries, solid electrolytes, photovoltaic and light-emitting devices, and luminescent materials. Functional applications of MOFs and porous frameworks.
